telemetry/manager.py:R5:_project_event_f: `isinstance(event, RowCreated)` is a nominal check against a concrete class ELSPETH defines (`elspeth.contracts.events.RowCreated`, `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)`), on a Tier-1 value the engine constructed itself — the ADR-032 sanctioned form, not a Tier-3 shape guard. It is load-bearing as `isinstance` specifically, and `type(event) is RowCreated` would be a security regression: this projection exists to strip row-derived fingerprints (`content_hash`) before any event reaches a telemetry observer or exporter, and it fails closed by collapsing the event to the exact owned base contract. A future `RowCreated` subclass carrying extra hash-bearing metadata is caught by `isinstance` and rebuilt from the five explicitly copied base fields with `content_hash=None`; under an identity check it would miss both arms and fall through to `return event`, egressing row content hashes verbatim. The else-branch is therefore not a don't-care: it is the path every non-row event legitimately takes, and the subclass-catching semantics are what keep it safe.

`isinstance(event, TransformCompleted)` is the second arm of the same egress projection and carries the same justification as the `RowCreated` arm above: a nominal check against a concrete owned `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)` in `elspeth.contracts.events`, applied to a Tier-1 event the engine constructed. It protects `input_hash`/`output_hash` — row-derived fingerprints that must never reach a telemetry observer or exporter — by rebuilding the event from its eight explicitly copied base fields with both hashes set to `None`. `isinstance` rather than `type(...) is ...` is deliberate and fail-closed: an unknown subclass adding hash-bearing metadata is collapsed to the known base contract instead of being trusted to redact itself, whereas an identity check would let it fall through to `return event` with fingerprints intact. Widening this to a structural/Protocol check is banned by ADR-032; the point of the check is nominal ownership.

Its contract is best-effort observation of an already-audited event: Landscape is the legal record and telemetry is emitted after it, so an observer defect must never break a row or kill the pipeline thread. Re-raising is precisely the behaviour this isolation forbids, and narrowing the clause is not available either — the callable is arbitrary operator code, so the exception type is unbounded and any narrowing would leak an unanticipated observer bug into the caller's row. `@observation_boundary` cannot cover this: its `BoundaryRule` vocabulary is `Literal["R1", "R5"]` and does not reach R4. The loop also continues to the remaining observers and to the exporters, so one broken observer degrades only its own projection.
telemetry/manager.py:R2:_exporter_delive: `getattr(exporter, "delivery_metrics", _DELIVERY_METRICS_ABSENT)` is an ADR-032 Tier-3 parse of an OPTIONAL capability on a third-party object: exporters arrive from external pluggy plugins via `elspeth_get_exporters` with no type gate in front of them, so the presence of `delivery_metrics` is genuinely unknown and absence is a legitimate answer that every caller already handles by treating `None` as 'this exporter does not report delivery metrics'. A malformed exporter is therefore loud, not ignored: raised from the export thread, `_export_loop` stores the exception and `flush()` re-raises it. The sentinel is a module-level `object()`, so no legitimate attribute value can collide with 'absent'.
